topics.label: Lecture introduction and overview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic introduces the lecturer, establishes the lecture's place within the course, and outlines the session's focus on the initiation and resolution of inflammation.

topics.label: Innate recognition of infection and damage through pattern recognition receptors
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the molecular basis of innate immune sensing, detailing how microbial and damage signals are detected by pattern recognition receptor families, their signaling cascades, and the inflammasome.

topics.label: Cellular inflammatory responses, leukocyte recruitment, and systemic complications
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics describe the cellular actions triggered during inflammation, including sentinel cell activation, leukocyte recruitment and tissue extravasation, lymphatic trafficking, and the pathology of septic shock when activation becomes systemic.

topics.label: Resolution of inflammation, tissue repair, and chronic inflammatory outcomes
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the active and passive mechanisms that shut down inflammation and promote tissue repair, as well as the chronic inflammation and granuloma formation that occur when resolution fails.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic wraps up the lecture and previews the next topic.
